title: Lenny on how he built his newsletter and podcast: follow pull, stay lean, iterate
summary: Lenny's wife Michelle Rial interviews him on how he went from Airbnb to a 1.2M-subscriber newsletter. He covers following pull over a plan, committing weekly using the Lindy effect, sourcing advice from practitioners, staying lean with no full-time employees, and heavy iteration. Also includes a fraud lesson from an overly generous launch.

principles.text: Pursue what you enjoy and others value; that overlap is rare, so follow the pull even without a plan.
principles.quote: Which is very rare, that Venn diagram of things. Just like, how often do you enjoy something and people value it?

principles.text: Use the Lindy effect: how long you've sustained a consistent habit signals you can keep it up, so commit weekly.
principles.quote: I've been doing this every week for 9 months. Which means I could probably do this for 9 more months.

principles.text: The best content comes from practitioners doing the real thing, not people pontificating from the clouds.
principles.quote: that's the source of the best advice is from practitioners doing the thing for real.

principles.text: Stay lean: avoid full-time employees and complexity so you don't build a job you hate.
principles.quote: I also am trying very hard to never have full-time employees. I'm trying to keep things really simple

principles.text: Quality comes from relentless iteration; he rewrites each newsletter post around 50 times before editors touch it.
principles.quote: when I write a newsletter post, I go through it probably, let's say 50 times making it better.

principles.text: An offer that's too generous attracts fraudsters; stress-test your free perks and APIs for abuse before launch.
principles.quote: that was way too good an offer. People came for it. Bad people.
